🚨🇲🇽 <u>"TO THE VICTOR GO THE SPOILS": TRUMP BOASTS OF TAKING VENEZUELA'S OIL</u>

Two ways to treat Venezuela. Mexico sends Navy aid ships and solidarity, no conditions attached. The US just takes the oil.

"We're taking a lot of oil from Venezuela, billions and billions of barrels. To the victor belong the spoils, right?" — Trump said it on a stage in Las Vegas. Pillage as policy, out loud.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO AMONG THE HARDEST HIT BY LATIN AMERICA'S BIRTHRATE COLLAPSE: ECLAC</u>

A new ECLAC (Cepal) study puts Mexico above the regional average, with births set to fall 19.3%. Latin America went from a peak of 12 million births a year in the mid-90s to a projected 7.6 million — 13 countries are already below the 2.1 replacement rate.

The region built on cheap young labor now has to plan for aging. Pensions, healthcare, dignified work — exactly what the 4T has been building.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>AI ADOPTION LIFTS MEXICAN OUTPUT BY UP TO 45.8%</u>

Mexican firms using artificial intelligence produce up to 45.8% more — that's the association found in the electricity sector by three Centro México Digital studies built on INEGI's 2024 Economic Census. In finance the boost reaches 28.4%, in media and telecom 12.5%.

The catch: adoption covers just 8% of firms nationally and 4.8% in manufacturing — versus 10% in the US and 63.3% in South Korean finance. Large companies adopt 3.5 times more than small ones.

And the upside isn't job cuts: across the whole economy, AI adoption is associated with 3.3% MORE employment per firm — technology complementing skilled work, not replacing it. (Data: El Economista)

⚖️🇲🇽 <u>VERACRUZ STRIPS MAYOR'S IMMUNITY — HE FLEES BEFORE THE VOTE</u>

The Veracruz state congress voted 40-8 to strip the constitutional fuero of Bertín Bravo Montero, mayor of Úrsulo Galván, so prosecutors can investigate him over the forced disappearance of businessman Héctor Ramos Sánchez — missing since May 14 — and his escort Ignacio López.

The mayor walked out of the legislative palace before the dictamen was even read, with prosecutor's vehicles stationed outside. His registered substitute, Pedro de Jesús Rosado Guzmán, will be sworn in to keep the municipality running.

An opposition mayor facing a disappearance case, immunity lifted by an overwhelming vote in a closed session: in Veracruz, the fuero no longer means impunity.

🇲🇽🌳 <u>MEXICO TO PLANT 6.6 MILLION TREES IN A SINGLE DAY</u>

On August 9, 235,000 people across all 32 states will plant more than 6.6 million trees and plants over 32,000 hectares — with drones dispersing pelleted seeds across 621 municipalities and 37 protected natural areas.

The Jornada Nacional de Reforestación is backed by 417,000 Sembrando Vida beneficiaries, Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, Sedena and Semar — part of a national strategy to reforest or conserve 1.5 billion trees by 2030.

Semarnat chief Alicia Bárcena framed the stakes: 70% of Mexico's territory has forest cover holding 12% of the planet's biodiversity — while 204,000 hectares are lost to deforestation every year.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO INE: YOUR 36-BILLION-PESO ASK IS "EXAGGERATED"</u>

Mexico's electoral institute wants 36,119 million pesos for 2027 — about 15 billion more than the entire 2024 federal election cost, even though 2024 also printed ballots for president and senators.

"Consideramos que, en todo caso, debería costar lo que costó la del 24, actualizado con la inflación... No entendemos por qué deba costar más," Sheinbaum said at her morning conference.

The INE's draft sets aside 17,395 million for its "project portfolio" plus a 4,687-million precautionary fund — for an election whose 176,741 polling stations are barely 6,500 more than in 2024.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>UNAM FIRES EXAM CONTRACTOR, ORDERS FULL AUDIT</u>

UNAM terminated its contract with Territorium Life ahead of schedule after the anomalies that wrecked its online admission exam — and opened both a technological audit and an internal audit of the contracting process itself.

The university paid the firm 69.2 million pesos: 27.2 million for the exam of 103,221 high school applicants and 41.9 million for the 158,558 licenciatura aspirants. The 58,000 rejected candidates will now take a new, in-person test.

"No tenemos interés en proteger a la empresa, pero tampoco culpar sin argumentos jurídicos," said UNAM's general counsel Hugo Concha Cantú — the audit will assign responsibility before any fine is claimed.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US PUTS $102 MILLION IN BOUNTIES ON CJNG LEADERS</u>

Washington escalated its offensive against the CJNG: the State Department now offers up to $102 million for information leading to the arrest or conviction of eight alleged leaders and operators of the Mexican cartel.

The bounty on Juan Carlos Valencia, "El Pelón" — who took over after El Mencho's death — rose to $25 million. "El Jardinero," "El Sapo" and "El Chorro" are worth $15 million each. Another 65 relatives and associates lost their US visas; 93 have been canceled since June 2025 under Executive Order 14059.

Bounties, visa bans, terrorist designations — the same DEA playbook for 50 years. Meanwhile Mexico's own numbers keep moving: homicides fell 18% in 2025 to a rate of 21.4 per 100,000, the steepest drop on record.

🇲🇽🔥🌐 Washington wants Mexico to wall off Chinese steel — while keeping a 50% tariff on Mexican steel

The double standard is the whole story. As the US finalizes — in the first week of August — the criteria for a new Section 301 “excess-capacity” probe aimed at China, it’s pressuring Mexico to match Washington’s levies on Chinese steel and aluminum. Meanwhile the US keeps its own 50% Section 232 tariff clamped on Mexican steel — even though Mexico is the single largest buyer of US steel.

Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard’s answer: cut that 50% down to about 10%, the same rate Washington already handed the United Kingdom. Mexico already applies up to 25% duties plus anti-dumping measures on Chinese steel under its own 2023 decree — on its own terms, for its own industry, not on command.

“Free trade” for thee, protectionism for me. Mexico’s play: trade the alignment Washington demands for the fairness Mexico is owed — and keep every other door open.

🇲🇽🐉🌐 Mexico to Beijing: diversify, yes — but trade has to run both ways

After a working visit to Beijing, Mexico has publicly told its No. 2 trading partner to move toward “more balanced” trade. The numbers explain why: in 2025 China took just 1.5% of Mexico’s exports ($9.03B) while supplying 19.8% of its imports ($120.15B) — a net deficit of $111.1 billion in a single year.

This is what sovereignty looks like in a multipolar world. Mexico refuses to be anyone’s captive market — not Washington’s, not Beijing’s. It keeps the China channel open (investment and machinery on the table) while demanding reciprocity: the same access for Mexican exporters in China that Chinese firms enjoy here. Beijing has since pledged to work toward balance.

The tariff reform in force since Jan. 1 — 1,463 lines, duties of 5–50% — isn’t about “picking a side.” It’s leverage. A country that multiplies its options gets to set terms instead of taking them.
